result.markdown: --- title: "Session 3 — Comparing Survival: the Log-Rank Test" subtitle: "Null hypothesis · observed vs expected · stratified log-rank · wrong tests · Lab 3" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 2: Kaplan-Meier curves by group - Today: **are the curves different** beyond chance? - By the end you can: - run and read a **log-rank test** - use **observed vs expected** deaths to give the direction - **stratify** a log-rank test - explain why a **t-test of follow-up time** is wrong ::: # Topic 1 — The log-rank test {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## What it compares At every event time, given how many are at risk in each group, how many deaths would we **expect** in each group **if the curves were the same**? The test adds up (observed − expected) over all event times. ::: {.key} **H₀:** the survival curves (hazards) are the **same** in all groups. Small p: evidence of a **difference somewhere along follow-up**. It uses the **whole curve**, and is most powerful when the hazards are **proportional**. ::: ## HIV status ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lr_hiv <- survdiff(Surv(time_months, status) ~ hiv, data = tb) lr_hiv ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: survdiff(formula = Surv(time_months, status) ~ hiv, data = tb) N Observed Expected (O-E)^2/E (O-E)^2/V hiv=Negative 537 94 101.6 0.565 5.6 hiv=Positive 63 19 11.4 5.022 5.6 Chisq= 5.6 on 1 degrees of freedom, p= 0.02 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Observed** vs **expected** deaths: HIV-positive patients had more deaths than expected (19 vs 11.4) - `Chisq` on **1 df** and its p-value: here p = 0.018 - The test gives **no size of effect**: use the hazard ratio (Session 4) ::: ## A null result ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lr_sex <- survdiff(Surv(time_months, status) ~ sex, data = tb) c(chisq = round(lr_sex$chisq, 2), p = round(1 - pchisq(lr_sex$chisq, 1), 2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` chisq p 0.23 0.63 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.warn} p = 0.63 means **no evidence** of a difference by sex, **not proof** of none: look at the **CI of the hazard ratio** to see which differences remain plausible. ::: # Topic 2 — Getting it right {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Stratified log-rank Compare HIV groups **within** treatment arms, then combine: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} survdiff(Surv(time_months, status) ~ hiv + strata(treatment), data = tb) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: survdiff(formula = Surv(time_months, status) ~ hiv + strata(treatment), data = tb) N Observed Expected (O-E)^2/E (O-E)^2/V hiv=Negative 537 94 102.1 0.639 6.64 hiv=Positive 63 19 10.9 5.966 6.64 Chisq= 6.6 on 1 degrees of freedom, p= 0.01 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Use when another variable also affects survival and is **unbalanced** between the groups - It cannot compare the stratifying variable itself, and **adjusts for one factor at a time**: for several, use Cox ::: ## More than two groups ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tb |> mutate(group = case_when(mdr_tb == "Yes" ~ "MDR-TB", hiv == "Positive" ~ "HIV, drug-sensitive", TRUE ~ "Drug-sensitive, HIV-negative")) |> survdiff(Surv(time_months, status) ~ group, data = _) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: survdiff(formula = Surv(time_months, status) ~ group, data = mutate(tb, group = case_when(mdr_tb == "Yes" ~ "MDR-TB", hiv == "Positive" ~ "HIV, drug-sensitive", TRUE ~ "Drug-sensitive, HIV-negative"))) N Observed Expected (O-E)^2/E (O-E)^2/V group=Drug-sensitive, HIV-negative 484 78 92.03 2.14 11.56 group=HIV, drug-sensitive 61 18 11.26 4.04 4.49 group=MDR-TB 55 17 9.71 5.48 6.01 Chisq= 11.7 on 2 degrees of freedom, p= 0.003 ``` ::: ::: An **overall** test on k groups has **k − 1 df**; it says *some* group differs. Follow with pairwise comparisons, **adjusted** for multiple testing. ## The wrong tests ::: {.bad} - **t-test or Wilcoxon on follow-up time:** mixes deaths and censored times, and answers a different question - **Chi-square on "died yes/no"** ignores follow-up time, which differs between patients ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(t_test = signif(t.test(time_months ~ hiv, data = tb)$p.value, 2), log_rank = signif(1 - pchisq(lr_hiv$chisq, 1), 2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` t_test log_rank 0.300 0.018 ``` ::: ::: ## The log-rank test does not ::: {.incremental} - **Adjust** for several covariates: use **Cox regression** - Give an **effect size**: report the **hazard ratio with a CI** - Work well when the **curves cross**: then the "average" difference can be near zero while the curves differ early and late ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 3 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `survival-workshop/labs/lab3_logrank.R` - `survdiff()` by HIV, sex and MDR-TB - observed vs expected, the p-value from the chi-square - `strata()` and the wrong t-test ::: **Time:** 30 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s3q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="jtwbia.so757r" data-show="VGhlIHN1cnZpdmFsIGN1cnZlcyBhcmUgdGhlIHNhbWUgaW4gYm90aCBncm91cHM=" data-explain="VGhlIGxvZy1yYW5rIHRlc3QgYXNrcyB3aGV0aGVyIHRoZSB0d28gc3Vydml2YWwgKGhhemFy ZCkgY3VydmVzIGNvaW5jaWRlIG92ZXIgdGhlIHdob2xlIGZvbGxvdy11cC4gSXQgZG9lcyBu b3QgY29tcGFyZSBvbmx5IGEgbWVkaWFuIG9yIG9uZSB0aW1lIHBvaW50Lg=="} What is the null hypothesis of the log-rank test comparing two groups? - The median survival time is the same in both groups - The numbers of patients at the start are equal in both groups - The survival curves are the same in both groups - The hazard ratio is exactly 1 at one particular time ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s3q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="jtwoqy.so7jp3" data-show="TW9yZSBkZWF0aHMgdGhhbiBleHBlY3RlZCBpZiBzdXJ2aXZhbCB3ZXJlIHRoZSBzYW1lIGlu IGJvdGggZ3JvdXBz" data-explain="RXhwZWN0ZWQgZGVhdGhzIGFyZSB3aGF0IHRoZSBncm91cCB3b3VsZCBoYXZlIGlmIHRoZSBj dXJ2ZXMgd2VyZSBpZGVudGljYWwuIEEgZ3JvdXAgd2l0aCBtb3JlIGRlYXRocyB0aGFuIGV4 cGVjdGVkIGZhcmVkIHdvcnNlIHRoYW4gdGhlIHBvb2xlZCBleHBlcmllbmNlLg=="} HIV-positive patients had 19 observed deaths and 11.4 expected. How should this be read? - Fewer deaths than expected if survival were the same in both groups - More deaths than expected if survival were the same in both groups - The test has failed, because the two numbers are different - A difference of 7.6 deaths per 100 person-years ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s3q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="jtx1zo.so7y6h" data-show="Rm9sbG93LXVwIHRpbWVzIG1peCBkZWF0aHMgYW5kIGNlbnNvcmVkIHRpbWVzLCBzbyBpdCBh c2tzIHRoZSB3cm9uZyBxdWVzdGlvbg==" data-explain="Q2Vuc29yZWQgdGltZXMgYXJlIG5vdCBkZWF0aCB0aW1lcywgc28gY29tcGFyaW5nIGF2ZXJh Z2UgZm9sbG93LXVwIHRpbWVzIGRvZXMgbm90IGNvbXBhcmUgc3Vydml2YWwuIFRoZSBsb2ct cmFuayB0ZXN0IHVzZXMgdGhlIGNlbnNvcmluZyBpbmZvcm1hdGlvbiBjb3JyZWN0bHku"} Why is a t-test on the follow-up time of two groups inappropriate for survival data? - The t-test needs both of the groups to have the same number of patients - Follow-up times follow a normal distribution in a typical sample of patients - Follow-up times mix deaths and censored times, so it asks the wrong question - A t-test can be used for yes/no outcomes and not for times to an event ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s3q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="jtxf8e.so8cnv" data-show="Tm8gZXZpZGVuY2Ugb2YgYSBkaWZmZXJlbmNlIGluIHN1cnZpdmFsIGJ5IHNleCBpbiB0aGlz IGNvaG9ydA==" data-explain="QSBsYXJnZSBwLXZhbHVlIGlzIHdlYWsgZXZpZGVuY2UgYWdhaW5zdCAnbm8gZGlmZmVyZW5j ZScsIG5vdCBwcm9vZiBvZiBlcXVhbGl0eS4gVGhlIGhhemFyZCByYXRpbyBhbmQgaXRzIENJ IHNob3cgd2hpY2ggZGlmZmVyZW5jZXMgYXJlIHN0aWxsIHBsYXVzaWJsZS4="} The log-rank test by sex gives p = 0.63. Which conclusion is best? - Men and women have been shown to have identical survival in the cohort - Sex has no effect on survival in any population of TB patients - The test was underpowered, so it should be repeated on more patients - No evidence of a difference in survival by sex in this cohort ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s3q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="jtxsh0.so8r55" data-show="V2hlbiBhbm90aGVyIGZhY3RvciBhZmZlY3RzIHN1cnZpdmFsIGFuZCBpcyB1bmJhbGFuY2Vk IGJldHdlZW4gZ3JvdXBz" data-explain="U3RyYXRpZmljYXRpb24gY29tcGFyZXMgZ3JvdXBzIHdpdGhpbiBsZXZlbHMgb2YgYW5vdGhl ciB2YXJpYWJsZSBhbmQgY29tYmluZXMgdGhlIHJlc3VsdHMsIHNvIGltYmFsYW5jZSBpbiB0 aGF0IHZhcmlhYmxlIGRvZXMgbm90IGRpc3RvcnQgdGhlIGNvbXBhcmlzb24u"} When is a stratified log-rank test most useful? - When another factor affects survival and is unbalanced between groups - When the survival curves of the two groups cross over each other once - When there are no deaths recorded in one of the two groups compared - When the follow-up times of the patients are normally distributed ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Log-rank**: compares the whole curves; H₀ = same survival - **Observed vs expected** deaths give the direction - Stratify for **one** other factor; use **Cox** for several - Never t-test follow-up times; a non-significant p is not proof of no difference ::: **Next:** Session 4: Cox regression

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
